source.extraction: First HTML pre block; remove HTML tags, HTML-unescape once, UTF-8 encode; preserve leading and trailing whitespace.

differences: C stores the initial LCG state in a function-static long; YIAN passes one owned i64 seed by reference from main. Both update it with the same IA/IC/IM recurrence and return maximum*seed/IM in the same floating-point operation order.
Both replace each entry probability with the running sum in source order; YIAN uses u8 symbols and f64 fields in AminoAcid.
Both draw one LCG value and use the same lower-bound binary-search decisions over cumulative probabilities.
Both emit the record header and generated sequence in lines of at most 60 symbols. YIAN writes bytes through a buffered Stdout writer and carries the RNG state explicitly.
C copies ALU into a temporary mutable NUL-terminated buffer; YIAN uses a byte-slice offset modulo the same 287-byte source sequence to emit identical 60-column lines.
C reads n from argv; YIAN selects n through its bench-scale marker, with full/fast values 25000000/100000.
Both build the official IUB and Homo sapiens probability tables and emit ONE(2n), TWO(3n), THREE(5n) in that order; random generation continues from the TWO stream into THREE.
C has static probability arrays and output calls; YIAN uses owned dynamic amino-acid arrays and an 8192-byte buffered writer, then releases owned state.
